3R replication script (analysis.R)

How to replicate: save the block below as analysis.R, place cleaned.csv (in the export bundle) beside it, then run Rscript analysis.R. The script prints every table shown in the app; the app's numbers were verified byte-for-byte against native R output. Package citations are in section 6.
# Reproducible analysis script generated by Telos
# Run from the folder holding cleaned.csv. Uncomment install.packages() the first time.
# install.packages(c("ggplot2"))
library(ggplot2)
d <- read.csv("cleaned.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
d[["teaching_method"]] <- factor(d[["teaching_method"]])
d[["passed_course"]] <- factor(d[["passed_course"]])

# === 01 · Chi-square independence ===
sub <- d[!is.na(d[["teaching_method"]]) & trimws(d[["teaching_method"]]) != "" & !is.na(d[["passed_course"]]) & trimws(d[["passed_course"]]) != "", ]
tab <- table(sub[["teaching_method"]], sub[["passed_course"]])
g <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(tab, correct = TRUE))
print(g)
print(g$expected)
print(prop.table(tab, 1) * 100)
print(prop.table(tab, 2) * 100)
cat("Cramer's V:", sqrt(unname(suppressWarnings(chisq.test(tab, correct = FALSE))$statistic) / (sum(tab) * (min(dim(tab)) - 1))), "\n")
print(ggplot(sub, aes(teaching_method, fill = passed_course)) + geom_bar(position = "dodge"))

\section{Chi-square independence}

\begin{tabular}{llll}
\toprule
Row \textbackslash{} Column & No & Yes & Total \\
\midrule

Flipped & 17 [29.00] (21.3\% / 19.5\%) r=$-$3.42 & 63 [51.00] (78.8\% / 41.2\%) r=3.42 & 80 \\
Lecture & 40 [29.00] (50.0\% / 46.0\%) r=3.13 & 40 [51.00] (50.0\% / 26.1\%) r=$-$3.13 & 80 \\
Total & 87 & 153 & 240 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\begin{tabular}{llll}
\toprule
$\chi$\textsuperscript{2} & df & p & Cram\'{e}r's V [95\% CI] \\
\midrule
14.39 & 2 & $<$.001 & 0.24 [0.13, 1.00] \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\includegraphics{figures/01_chi-square-independence/figure_bar.png}

Tests whether two categorical variables are associated. A p below alpha means they are related; Cram\'{e}r's V gives the strength of association (0--1); each cell's standardized residual (r) beyond about $\pm$1.96 flags a category combination that significantly drives the association. Valid only when expected counts are mostly $\ge$ 5 (the app flags this and suggests Fisher's exact) and each case appears once (raw counts, not percentages). Your significance threshold ($\alpha$) is 0.05.

A chi-square test of independence gave $\chi$\textsuperscript{2}(2, N=240)=14.39, p $<$ .001, V=.24 [.13, 1.00].

Statistical basis: Chi-square test of independence (Pearson, K. (1900). "On the criterion that a given system of deviations from the probable in the case of a correlated system of variables is such that it can be reasonably supposed to have arisen from random sampling." Philosophical Magazine, 50(302), 157-175.); Cram\'{e}r's V effect size (w-family; Cohen, 1988) (Cohen, J. (1988). Statistical Power Analysis for the Behavioral Sciences (2nd ed.). Routledge.).

\end{document}

# 23 · Chi-square independence

**Question:** are two categorical variables related?

**Scenario:** Campus study: is teaching method related to pass/fail?

## Input configuration

- **Dataset:** `campus-study.csv`
- **Configure-data:** app defaults (auto-detected types/levels)
- **Options:** continuity correction ON (2×2 only); α 0.05

**Role assignments** (drag column → slot):

| Column | Role slot |
|---|---|
| `teaching_method` | row variable |
| `passed_course` | column variable |
